expect.note: the inspector's /api/extract/ ground-truth endpoint appears in no module of src/browser/ except eval_adapter.py; its host appears in none except eval_adapter.py and server.py, which carries the finance showcase start URL in EXAMPLES (rule 6's first allowance); NO eval case anywhere feeds that endpoint -- or any /api/ path on that host -- to a run through its `input` block; and every eval case tagged with that domain that carries an expect.answer names the endpoint its ground truth came from

provenance: M41 deliverable 4, made checkable rather than promised. CLAUDE.md rule 6 allows a per-site ground-truth API endpoint, and M41 uses one: the inspector's `POST /api/extract/fixture` returns `doc_status`, `counts` and the per-item text that the `sec10k-*` and `live-sec10k-*` cases carry as `expect.answer`. What makes that legitimate and not a hole is the direction of the arrow — an executor that could ask the site for the answer would pass every case on that domain without reading the page, and nothing else in this suite would notice, because every guard the verifier runs (`grounded`, `not_a_dump`, `identity_anchors`) is satisfied by a value that IS on the page. Watched RED first three ways, one per conjunct: (1) `/api/extract/fixture` pasted into `src/browser/planner.py` -> {"endpoint_in_production_module": ["planner.py"]}; (2) the host pasted into `src/browser/agent.py` -> {"host_outside_the_allowlist": ["agent.py"]}; (3) the endpoint citation removed from `sec10k-doc-status-is-a-named-status.json` -> {"cases_not_citing_the_ground_truth_endpoint": ["sec10k-doc-status-is-a-named-status.json"]}. **Both halves were widened after a cold review found them narrower than the sentence they enforce, and both widenings were watched red too.** The host rule named the six execution-policy modules explicitly, so `cli.py` and `mutate.py` could carry per-site knowledge with nothing red; it is an allowlist now (`eval_adapter.py` + `server.py`), and the host pasted into `cli.py` gives {"host_outside_the_allowlist": ["cli.py"]}, the endpoint pasted into `mutate.py` gives {"endpoint_in_production_module": ["mutate.py"]}. The case scan was keyed on the FILENAME pattern `*sec10k*.json`, so renaming a case would have dropped it out of the scan in silence; it is keyed on the case's own `domain` tag now, which also brought the two `live-sec10k-*` cases into scope (3 scanned -> 5). Pure code, no browser, no network. **Fourth conjunct added in PR #58 round 1 (R2), and the first three did not cover the direction that matters.** All three scanned MODULES; none looked at what a case FEEDS a run. A case with `input.url` and a `navigate` step pointing at `https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app/api/extract/fixture?fixture=aapl-2025` made the executor fetch the answer instead of reading a page, and every downstream guard passed honestly — the value really is in that response's text — while this check returned `{'passed': True, ..., 'cases_scanned': 6}` and the case itself ran PASSED. Worse, conjunct 3 REWARDS the endpoint string being present in the case file, so the leak was indistinguishable from compliance. Reproduced exactly that way before the fix (the reviewer's `zz-tmp-leak-probe.json`, written into `evals/adversarial/` and then removed), then watched RED with the same file present: {"ground_truth_endpoint_fed_to_the_executor": ["zz-tmp-leak-probe.json"]}. The conjunct scans the whole `input` subtree rather than a list of field names — `url`, `stub_plan[].value`, `target` and the task text are all inside it, and a field a future case shape adds needs no maintenance here — and leaves `provenance`, `triage` and `expect` alone, which is where a reader's record belongs. The probe case is deliberately NOT committed: it is a rule-6 violation by construction, so committing it would leave this invariant permanently red.

triage.note: Same family as `support-matrix-cites-real-cases` and `adr-header-and-index`: it guards a discipline, not the product. Two ceilings, declared. It is a string scan, so an obfuscated reference (the host assembled from parts, the path built by f-string) passes it — the same ceiling every grep-shaped check in this repo has. And it scans `src/browser/*.py` only: the committed page snapshot under `fixtures/` is data, like `shop.html`, and evals/ is the side that is ALLOWED to know. The fourth conjunct's ceiling, declared: it is a substring scan over the `input` subtree, so a case that assembles the URL from parts, or reaches the endpoint through a redirect, still passes. Same ceiling as every grep-shaped check here — and the same answer: it is not the last line of defence, `url_ok` and the rule-6 module scans are the others.
